h: Jewels, gardens and climbing in Brum
p: First climb nerves are completely normal, and the good news is that most kids lose them within a couple of walls. A good trick is to let go from just a little way up on the first attempt, feel the auto-belay lower you gently, and then go higher each time after that. Short nails, no rings and pockets emptied make life easier, and if your climber has long hair, tie it back. It's worth a light snack beforehand rather than a big meal.

After the session, the Jewellery Quarter is a fascinating part of Birmingham to explore, with workshops, independent shops and the Museum of the Jewellery Quarter, which preserves an old family workshop exactly as it was left. The Library of Birmingham in Centenary Square is free to visit and has rooftop terraces with views across the city.

Fancy a breath of fresh air? Birmingham Botanical Gardens in Edgbaston has glasshouses, gardens and a play area, and it's a calm contrast to an hour of climbing. Digbeth, east of the centre, has street art and the Custard Factory with its quirky shops and food, great for teens and adults who want something a bit different. Grand Central above New Street station is handy for food if you're getting the train. Whichever route you take, Birmingham makes it easy to turn a climb into a full day out, rain or shine.
